requirement_text: 'Only foreign secondary school-leaving diplomas with a broad curriculum (mainly literary or scientific) give access to the bachelor's programmes', subject to average requirements and supplementary entrance examinations. Critically, 'the mere fact that a diploma gives access to university studies in the country that awarded it is not sufficient to give access to UNIL' — home-country university eligibility is explicitly NOT sufficient on its own.
source_authority_note: unil.ch is University of Lausanne's official domain; not .edu/.ac./.gov.
researcher_notes: Important exclusion-style clause: this directly rules out a naive 'if it gets you into a university at home, it gets you into UNIL' assumption.

requirement_text: Mandatory diploma conditions: the certificate must be the highest secondary certificate awarded in its issuing country, obtained after a minimum of 12 years of study; obtained after completing at least 3 years of upper-secondary education from a complete (non-shortened) program at a recognized school; must grant general university access in the home country; and must be issued by a government body or authorized institution. Six subjects must be studied continuously over the final three years (language of instruction, second language, mathematics, an experimental science, a humanities subject, and an elective from philosophy/computer science/repeat categories), with general education comprising 'at least 90%' of curriculum content.
researcher_notes: CROSS-CHECK PERFORMED per coordinator instruction: this six-subject/90%-general-education structure matches the central swissuniversities framework (system file REQ-2026-08-21-0001) and UZH's/UNIGE's own restatements closely — no factual conflict found across all three institutions' own pages on this specific structural point.

requirement_text: CONDITIONAL RECOGNITION (verbatim shape, not a threshold): for diplomas combining study periods across different educational systems, the diploma is 'recognised only if the last three years have been successfully followed at upper secondary level' in the corresponding final years of the respective systems. Recognition is conditional on WHERE in the sequence the mixed schooling occurred, not on a grade or score.
researcher_notes: FLAGGED PER COORDINATOR INSTRUCTION as a genuine conditional-recognition rule distinct from both a numeric threshold and a supplementary-exam requirement — recorded verbatim as the structural condition it actually is (sequencing/continuity of the final three years), not collapsed into either other shape.

requirement_text: For candidates whose schooling was not through regular continuous enrollment during the final three years, an additional procedural condition applies: 'each subject must have been examined separately' — i.e. the six required subjects cannot be certified in aggregate/combined form for such candidates; each needs its own discrete examination record.
limitations: Applies specifically to non-regularly-enrolled candidates (e.g. homeschooled, external/private candidates); not a general rule for all applicants.
researcher_notes: A second, narrower conditional-recognition nuance layered on top of REQ-2026-08-21-0503 — kept as a separate record rather than merged, since it applies to a different subset of candidates (irregular enrollment) than the mixed-system-sequencing rule.

requirement_text: Applicants without French as a mother tongue and without a Swiss maturité must pass a French language test — minimum B1 level (CEFR) — before FINAL enrollment (not necessarily before the admission decision itself). Exemptions apply for holders of recognized French proficiency certificates (DELF B1/B2, DALF C1/C2, TCF, TEF, TELC, FIDE passport, or CQF) obtained within the three years prior to enrollment, or for candidates who completed one full academic year with 60+ ECTS at specified French-language institutions.
limitations: Note the B1 threshold here is UNIL's OWN general French requirement for non-native-French applicants, distinct from and lower than the C1-level French specifically required as one of the four mandatory ECUS exam subjects (see REQ-2026-08-21-0506) — these are two different requirements applying to different (sometimes overlapping) applicant populations, not a contradiction.

requirement_text: Applicants with an unequivalent foreign diploma must take the ECUS (Swiss University Complementary Exam). 'Four subjects are mandatory: French (C1 level), Mathematics, English, History (including introduction to law).' One additional subject from Physics, Chemistry, Biology, or Geography must be selected. This is a pass/fail supplementary examination, not a scalar score threshold on the underlying diploma.
researcher_notes: CROSS-CHECK PERFORMED per coordinator instruction: this subject list (French, Mathematics, English, History+law mandatory; one of Physics/Chemistry/Biology/Geography elective) matches the central swissuniversities ECUS description (system file REQ-2026-08-21-0005) exactly — no conflict found between UNIL's own restatement and the national swissuniversities description. Explicitly kept as a supplementary-exam requirement, not forced into a numeric-threshold shape.

requirement_text: Bachelor of Arts applicants require a basic Latin or Ancient Greek course if that language is absent from their secondary diploma, depending on the specific disciplines chosen within the degree.
limitations: Which specific disciplines within the BA trigger this was not enumerated in the extraction obtained.

program_name: Bachelor of Movement and Sport Sciences
requirement_text: A physical education exam must be successfully passed before studies begin in the Bachelor of Movement and Sport Sciences.
limitations: Exam format/content/dates not captured in this pass.

requirement_text: Only the first year of the Bachelor of Pharmacy is taught in Lausanne; mandatory transfer to the University of Geneva (UNIGE) is required for continued study.
researcher_notes: Notable structural fact: this is a genuinely joint UNIL/UNIGE program, not a standalone UNIL degree beyond year 1.

requirement_text: UNIL does NOT apply the EMS or a numerus clausus at first-year entry to the Bachelor in Medicine (BMed1) — enrollment is open to qualifying applicants. Foreign applicants must meet criteria set out in the 'Cantonal Regulation of 9 December 2020.' Progression from 1st to 2nd year (BMed2) instead happens via a competitive exam ('concours'): 'le passage en 2e année de Bachelor (BMed2) se fait sur concours depuis l'année académique 2022-2023' (progression to 2nd year has been via concours since the 2022-2023 academic year), a Vaud State Council decision that replaced an earlier propaedeutic-exam-with-threshold model and aligned UNIL with practices already used at Geneva and Neuchâtel.
source_authority_note: unil.ch official Faculty of Biology and Medicine domain; not .edu/.ac./.gov.
limitations: The 'Cantonal Regulation of 9 December 2020' governing foreign-applicant criteria for first-year entry was referenced but not independently fetched and read in full text during this pass — recommend a follow-up fetch of that specific regulation if precise foreign-applicant first-year criteria become decision-relevant for a specific student.
researcher_notes: IMPORTANT SHAPE DISTINCTION (per task brief and coordinator note): categorically different admission shape from ETH Zurich's/UZH's EMS-gated entry. See Switzerland-system file record REQ-2026-08-21-0010 for the cross-institutional summary; UNIL's and UNIGE's concours systems are structurally similar (both introduced as 1st-to-2nd-year competitive exams under cantonal/rectorate authorization) but on different timelines (UNIGE 2017-2018, UNIL 2022-2023) — recorded as distinct per-institution facts rather than merged into one generic 'French-speaking Switzerland' statement.

requirement_text: Concours (2nd-year progression) mechanics: students must pass all 5 first-year exams within the same academic year (minimum grade 4/6); the top-ranked students advance to BMed2, with the exact number set by UNIL leadership based on available capacity (UNIL committed to training 245 doctors/year under a 2017-2020 federal special program, a target reached starting 2025); non-selected students may repeat the entire first year once, retaking all 5 exams with no prior scores carried forward.
source_authority_note: unil.ch official Faculty of Biology and Medicine domain; not .edu/.ac./.gov.
limitations: The page did not specify initial BMed1 entry academic standards (only BMed2 progression rules) — first-year entry criteria for foreign applicants are governed separately by the Cantonal Regulation of 9 December 2020 referenced in REQ-2026-08-21-0510, which was not independently fetched.
